async function plan(input: AnswerInput, memories: Recalled[]) {
  const started = performance.now()
  const history = input.history
    .slice(-6)
    .map((m) => `${m.role === "user" ? "User" : "Assistant"}: ${m.text.slice(0, 1200)}`)
    .join("\n")
  const { result, choice } = await withFallback("planner", input.tracer, "plan", (c) =>
    generateText({
      model: model(c),
      providerOptions: reasoning(c),
      output: Output.object({ schema: PlanSchema }),
      instructions:
        "You are the Planner in a research assistant that answers from the user's own library of documents and recordings. If the latest question already stands alone, keep the user's own words as `standalone`; otherwise rewrite it minimally using the conversation. Then write search queries for the library: keywords and phrases its passages would contain, not questions.",
      prompt: `${memoryBlock(memories)}${history ? `Conversation so far:\n${history}\n\n` : ""}Latest question: ${input.question}`,
      abortSignal: input.abortSignal,
    }),
  )
  const out = result.output
  input.tracer.log({
    agent: "planner",
    step: "plan",
    action: "planned",
    model: choice.id,
    latencyMs: Math.round(performance.now() - started),
    tokens: { input: result.usage.inputTokens, output: result.usage.outputTokens },
    detail: out,
  })
  return { ...out, model: choice.id }
}

/** Embeds texts with Nemotron in batches, a few at once, each vector in its text's place. */
export async function embed(
  texts: string[],
  as: EmbedAs,
): Promise<{ vectors: number[][]; tokens: number }> {
  const batches: string[][] = []
  for (let i = 0; i < texts.length; i += INGEST.embeddingBatch) {
    batches.push(texts.slice(i, i + INGEST.embeddingBatch))
  }
  const replies: Reply[] = new Array(batches.length)
  let next = 0
  await Promise.all(
    Array.from({ length: Math.min(INGEST.embeddingParallel, batches.length) }, async () => {
      while (next < batches.length) {
        const n = next++
        replies[n] = await request(batches[n] as string[], as)
      }
    }),
  )
  const vectors = replies.flatMap((reply) =>
    [...reply.data].sort((a, b) => a.index - b.index).map((d) => d.embedding),
  )
  if (vectors.length !== texts.length) throw new Error("Embedding reply is missing vectors")
  const tokens = replies.reduce((sum, reply) => sum + (reply.usage?.total_tokens ?? 0), 0)
  return { vectors, tokens }
}

async function write(
  input: AnswerInput,
  question: string,
  sources: SourceRef[],
  feedback: string | null,
  onDelta?: (delta: string) => void,
  memories: Recalled[] = [],
) {
  const started = performance.now()
  const prompt =
    `${memoryBlock(memories)}Passages:\n${passagesBlock(sources)}\n\nQuestion: ${question}` +
    (feedback
      ? `\n\nYour previous draft was REJECTED by the Verifier:\n${feedback}\n\nRewrite the answer fixing every problem. Use only facts and exact quotes from the passages.`
      : "")
  const { result, choice } = await withFallback("writer", input.tracer, "write", async (c) => {
    if (!onDelta) {
      const r = await generateText({
        model: model(c),
        providerOptions: reasoning(c),
        instructions: WRITER_INSTRUCTIONS,
        prompt,
        abortSignal: input.abortSignal,
      })
      return { text: r.text, usage: r.usage }
    }
    const stream = streamText({
      model: model(c),
      providerOptions: reasoning(c),
      instructions: WRITER_INSTRUCTIONS,
      prompt,
      abortSignal: input.abortSignal,
    })
    // Only the answer streams: the caveat and the sources are read once the draft is done.
    let text = ""
    let sent = 0
    for await (const delta of stream.textStream) {
      text += delta
      const end = bodyEnd(text, false)
      if (end > sent) {
        onDelta(text.slice(sent, end))
        sent = end
      }
    }
    const end = bodyEnd(text, true)
    if (end > sent) onDelta(text.slice(sent, end))
    return { text, usage: await stream.usage }
  })
  input.tracer.log({
    agent: "writer",
    step: feedback ? "revise" : "draft",
    action: feedback ? "revised_answer" : "drafted_answer",
    model: choice.id,
    latencyMs: Math.round(performance.now() - started),
    tokens: { input: result.usage.inputTokens, output: result.usage.outputTokens },
  })
  return { text: result.text, model: choice.id }
}

async function verify(
  input: AnswerInput,
  draft: ParsedAnswer,
  sources: SourceRef[],
  round: number,
  missingDocs: Set<string>,
  memo: VerifyMemo,
): Promise<Verdict> {
  const started = performance.now()
  const byLabel = new Map(sources.map((s) => [s.label, s]))
  const lineByN = new Map(draft.sources.map((l) => [l.n, l]))
  const reasons: string[] = []
  const badQuotes = new Set<number>()
  const quoteReasons = new Map<number, string>()
  const supportReasons = new Map<number, string>()
  const failQuote = (n: number, why: string) => {
    badQuotes.add(n)
    reasons.push(why)
    quoteReasons.set(n, why)
  }

  // 1. Code check: each cited number has a source line whose quote is in that passage. A quote
  //    that is verbatim in a different given passage is moved there (the words are real; the
  //    label was wrong), so the citation opens where the words actually are.
  const used = [...new Set(draft.sentences.flatMap((s) => s.cites))]
  const keyOf = new Map(sources.map((src) => [src.label, quoteKey(src.text)]))
  for (const n of used) {
    const line = lineByN.get(n)
    const source = line && byLabel.get(line.label)
    if (!line || !source) {
      failQuote(n, `[${n}] has no source line naming one of the given passages`)
      continue
    }
    if (line.quote.split(/\s+/).length < 3) {
      failQuote(n, `[${n}] quote is too short to check: "${line.quote}"`)
      continue
    }
    const key = quoteKey(line.quote)
    if (keyOf.get(line.label)?.includes(key)) continue
    const actual = sources.find((src) => keyOf.get(src.label)?.includes(key))
    if (actual) {
      input.tracer.log({
        agent: "verifier",
        step: `verify_${round}`,
        action: "reattributed_quote",
        detail: { n, from: line.label, to: actual.label },
      })
      line.label = actual.label
    } else {
      failQuote(n, `[${n}] quote is not verbatim in ${line.label}: "${line.quote}"`)
    }
  }
  // Quotes from documents the Zetaris pre-check could not find are not evidence.
  for (const n of used) {
    const source = byLabel.get(lineByN.get(n)?.label ?? "")
    if (source && missingDocs.has(source.fileId) && !badQuotes.has(n)) {
      failQuote(n, `[${n}] cites a document that is not in the evidence store`)
    }
  }

/**
 * Each agent's Nemotron model (packages/models calls them), with a fallback on another model for an
 * outage or a malformed reply. Picked by the measured benchmark of testing on NVIDIA's API
 * (gen-ai/.spikes/costs/BENCHMARK.md, the same cases as the earlier models' run): Ultra with
 * thinking off was the only setup to pass everything (0/10 false rejections, 6/6 planted errors
 * caught, 9/9 quotes verbatim, citation format 3/3). Lightning reads and returns JSON well and
 * judges well when it thinks, but never wrote the cited format; Super 3.5 often answered 500.
 */
export const MODELS = {
  /** Plans the run: whether it needs the library, which queries, whether to compare. */
  planner: {
    primary: { ...ULTRA("off"), deadlineMs: 15_000, hedgeAfterMs: 5_000 },
    fallback: { ...LIGHTNING("off"), hedgeAfterMs: 4_000 },
  },
  /** Writes the cited answer: 9/9 quotes verbatim, refused the planted figure 3/3. */
  writer: { primary: { ...ULTRA("off"), hedgeAfterMs: 8_000 }, fallback: SUPER("off") },
  /** Support checks: 0/10 false rejections, 6/6 planted errors (Lightning thinking: the same). */
  verifier: { primary: { ...ULTRA("off"), hedgeAfterMs: 15_000 }, fallback: LIGHTNING("low") },
  /** Deep search: plans the paper and encyclopedia queries. */
  scout: { primary: { ...LIGHTNING("off"), hedgeAfterMs: 4_000 }, fallback: ULTRA("off") },
  /** Screens found sources against the question, batch by batch (Markovian steps). */
  screener: { primary: { ...ULTRA("off"), hedgeAfterMs: 12_000 }, fallback: LIGHTNING("low") },
  /** Claims and agreement across sources: the same strict-support judgement as the Verifier. */
  analyst: { primary: { ...ULTRA("off"), hedgeAfterMs: 15_000 }, fallback: LIGHTNING("low") },
  /**
   * Makes practice items from passages (F27); every answer key then goes to the Verifier. In the
   * background, and a draft is 600–950 tokens (13–27 s on Ultra, testing), so it gets longer.
   * Lightning drafted none that passed: vague keys, sentences not copied exactly.
   */
  tutor: {
    primary: { ...ULTRA("off"), deadlineMs: 90_000, hedgeAfterMs: 35_000 },
    fallback: { ...SUPER("off"), deadlineMs: 90_000 },
  },
  /** Reads a spoken ask that no pattern placed (S16): a one-line pick while you are still talking. */
  intent: {
    primary: { ...LIGHTNING("off"), deadlineMs: 8_000, hedgeAfterMs: 3_000 },
    fallback: ULTRA("off"),
  },
  /** Judges a typed answer the code check couldn't settle, with feedback that never gives it away. */
  grader: { primary: { ...ULTRA("off"), hedgeAfterMs: 10_000 }, fallback: LIGHTNING("low") },
} as const satisfies Record<string, { primary: ModelChoice; fallback: ModelChoice }>

/** Cache key: the same text, model, width and role is never embedded twice. */
export const embeddingKey = (text: string, as: EmbedAs) =>
  createHash("sha256")
    .update(`${INGEST.embeddingModel}\n${INGEST.embeddingDimensions}\n${as}\n${text}`)
    .digest("hex")

/**
 * Many pieces, packed into as few checks as fit (a whole article is one), so publishing isn't a
 * burst of calls. One retry each; `checked` is false only if a batch fails both times.
 */
export async function moderateAll(pieces: string[]): Promise<Moderation> {
  const batches: string[] = []
  for (const piece of pieces.map((p) => p.trim()).filter(Boolean)) {
    const last = batches.at(-1)
    if (last !== undefined && last.length + piece.length + 2 <= PUBLIC.moderationChars)
      batches[batches.length - 1] = `${last}\n\n${piece}`
    else batches.push(piece.slice(0, PUBLIC.moderationChars))
  }
  const categories = new Set<string>()
  let flagged = false
  for (const batch of batches) {
    let result: Moderation | null = null
    for (let attempt = 0; attempt < 2 && !result; attempt++) {
      if (attempt) await new Promise((resolve) => setTimeout(resolve, RETRY_AFTER_MS))
      result = await check(batch, BATCH_TIMEOUT_MS).catch(() => null)
    }
    if (!result) return { flagged, categories: [...categories], checked: false }
    flagged ||= result.flagged
    for (const c of result.categories) categories.add(c)
  }
  return { flagged, categories: [...categories], checked: true }
}

/**
 * Hedged requests ("The Tail at Scale", Dean and Barroso, 2013). NVIDIA's free tier answers most
 * calls in seconds but now and then holds one in its queue for minutes; the same request sent
 * again usually starts at once (in testing). So when the first attempt hasn't answered by `after`, a
 * second one goes out; whichever answers first wins and the other is cancelled.
 */
export function hedged<T>(options: {
  /** When the second attempt goes out; none when undefined. */
  after: number | undefined
  /** Stops every attempt (the caller's stop, or the call's deadline). */
  signal: AbortSignal
  attempt: (signal: AbortSignal) => Promise<T>
  /** Tidies up an attempt that answered after another had already won. */
  discard?: (value: T) => void
  onHedge?: () => void
}): Promise<T> {
  const { after, signal, attempt, discard, onHedge } = options
  return new Promise<T>((resolve, reject) => {
    const attempts: AbortController[] = []
    let settled = false
    let pending = 0
    let timer: ReturnType<typeof setTimeout> | undefined

    const finish = (winner: number | null) => {
      settled = true
      clearTimeout(timer)
      attempts.forEach((controller, i) => {
        if (i !== winner) controller.abort()
      })
    }
    const launch = () => {
      const controller = new AbortController()
      const index = attempts.push(controller) - 1
      pending++
      attempt(AbortSignal.any([signal, controller.signal])).then(
        (value) => {
          pending--
          if (settled) return discard?.(value)
          finish(index)
          resolve(value)
        },
        (error) => {
          pending--
          // A failure while another attempt is still running waits for that one; otherwise it
          // stands (the SDK retries server errors with backoff; a hedge is only for slowness).
          if (settled || pending > 0) return
          finish(null)
          reject(error)
        },
      )
    }

    launch()
    if (after !== undefined) {
      timer = setTimeout(() => {
        if (settled) return
        onHedge?.()
        launch()
      }, after)

/**
 * NVIDIA limits each model separately (in testing), so every model has its own bucket, shared by every call to it here.
 */
export function limiterFor(modelId: string): Limiter {
  let limiter = limiters.get(modelId)
  if (!limiter) {
    limiter = new Limiter(
      env.MODEL_REQUESTS_PER_MINUTE ?? LIMITS.modelRequestsPerMinute,
      LIMITS.modelCallsInFlight,
    )
    limiters.set(modelId, limiter)
  }
  return limiter
}

/**
 * The critique loop's rewrite (plan F12): only the sentences the Verifier rejected go back to
 * the Writer, with its reasons; every other sentence stays word for word. The Writer returns a
 * corrected sentence with its own quotes, or nothing, which drops it.
 */
async function reviseSentences(
  input: AnswerInput,
  draft: ParsedAnswer,
  rejected: { index: number; reasons: string[] }[],
  sources: SourceRef[],
) {
  const started = performance.now()
  const { result, choice } = await withFallback("writer", input.tracer, "revise", (c) =>
    generateText({
      model: model(c),
      providerOptions: reasoning(c),
      output: Output.object({ schema: FixSchema }),
      instructions: `${WRITER_INSTRUCTIONS}\n\nNow you are correcting single sentences the Verifier rejected. Fix each so every fact in it is stated in the passages it cites, or return an empty text to drop it. Do not touch other sentences.`,
      prompt: `Passages:\n${passagesBlock(sources)}\n\nAnswer so far:\n${draft.sentences
        .map((sn, i) => `(${i + 1}) ${sn.text}`)
        .join("\n")}\n\nRejected by the Verifier:\n${rejected
        .map((r) => `(${r.index + 1}) ${r.reasons.join("; ")}`)
        .join("\n")}`,
      abortSignal: input.abortSignal,
    }),
  )
  input.tracer.log({
    agent: "writer",
    step: "revise",
    action: "revised_sentences",
    model: choice.id,
    latencyMs: Math.round(performance.now() - started),
    tokens: { input: result.usage.inputTokens, output: result.usage.outputTokens },
    detail: { sentences: rejected.map((r) => r.index + 1) },
  })

  // Merge: replace each fixed sentence, giving its quotes fresh citation numbers.
  let next = Math.max(0, ...draft.sources.map((l) => l.n))
  const lines = [...draft.sources]
  const texts = draft.sentences.map((sn) => sn.text)
  const rewritten: string[] = []
  for (const fix of result.output.fixes) {
    const i = fix.sentence - 1
    if (texts[i] == null) continue
    if (!fix.text.trim()) {
      texts[i] = ""
      continue
    }
    const local = new Map<number, number>()
    for (const q of fix.quotes) {
      next++
      local.set(q.marker, next)
      lines.push({ n: next, label: q.passage.toLowerCase(), quote: q.quote })
    }
    // Models number the markers loosely: one that is neither this fix's own nor an existing
    // citation takes the next quote the fix gave and the text didn't use, rather than costing a
    // whole round as "no source line"; a fix with quotes but no markers gets them at its end.
    const markers = [...fix.text.matchAll(/\[(\d+)\]/g)].map((m) => Number(m[1]))
    const spare = [...local.entries()]
      .filter(([marker]) => !markers.includes(marker))

export const INGEST = {
  /** A page with fewer characters than this (and an image) is a scan and gets OCR (S00 rule). */
  scanCharsPerPage: 20,
  ocrImage: "jbarlow83/ocrmypdf-alpine:v17.13.0",
  ocrLanguages: "eng",
  ocrTimeoutMs: 10 * 60 * 1000,
  convertTimeoutMs: 2 * 60 * 1000,
  fetchTimeoutMs: 30_000,
  /** Sent with web and paper downloads; never a personal address. */
  userAgent: "KonkyoBot/1.0 (+https://konkyo.xyz)",
  /** Transcript passages close at a speaker change, a pause, or this length. */
  transcriptPassageSeconds: 45,
  transcriptPauseSeconds: 2.5,
  embeddingModel: NEMOTRON.embed,
  /**
   * Nemotron's vectors are 2048 wide; the API shortens and re-normalises them (Matryoshka). 1536
   * keeps most of the detail and stays under pgvector's 2000-dimension HNSW limit.
   */
  embeddingDimensions: 1536,
  embeddingBatch: 96,
  embeddingParallel: 2,
  transcriptionModel: "scribe_v2",
  /** Short file summaries: grounded writing, no reasoning needed. */
  summaryModel: NEMOTRON.lightning,
  /** OpenAlex lookups are a nicety; a slow answer must not hold a file back. */
  metadataTimeoutMs: 8_000,
} as const
